summary: "The Silent Witnesses" is a multimedia storytelling project developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars"). Using AI visual generation and video editing tools (Dreamina AI, Dola AI, and CapCut), we created two complementary assets—an anime-inspired comic strip and a cinematic short video—to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the historic NASA hardware left across the Moon and Mars and the science it made possible. Our project directly addresses the challenge by transforming technical mission history from the 1960s onward into accessible, engaging visual storytelling. By personifying lunar landers and Mars rovers with expressive faces and voices alongside dramatic space visuals, it helps young learners connect emotionally with equipment that is no longer active. This is important because it shifts how students view discarded spacecraft—showing that while their voices have faded, the data and technological breakthroughs they left behind continue to guide modern spaceflight and inspire the next generation of STEM explorers.
details: "The Silent Witnesses" is a multimedia storytelling project created for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars")that introduces school-age space enthusiasts to the historic hardware left across the solar system and the scientific discoveries it made possible. Using Dreamina AI, Dola AI, and CapCut for AI visual generation and video editing, our team combined two complementary formats—an anime-inspired comic strip and a cinematic short film—to trace NASA's exploration journey from 1960s lunar missions to modern Mars rovers. By creatively personifying landers and rovers with expressive personalitiesalongside dramatic visual pacing and clear, accessible language, the project turns technical mission history into an emotionally engaging story that accommodates different learning styles. Ultimately, our intended impact is to show young learners that even though these pioneering machines are now silent, their data continues to drive modern spaceflight—inspiring future generations to dream bigger and pursue STEM.
